blocks.content: Everything a container writes lands in its own thin layer, and that layer is deleted with the container. Anything you intend to keep has to live outside it.

items: Named volumes: Docker manages the storage, best for databases
Bind mounts: a host path straight into the container, best for local development
tmpfs: memory only, never touches disk

blocks.content:
# Named volume, managed by Docker
docker run -v pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data postgres:17

# Bind mount, your working copy live in the container
docker run -v "$PWD":/app node:22-alpine

blocks.title: Bind mounts shadow the image
blocks.content: Mounting over /app hides whatever the image put there, including an installed node_modules. That is the usual cause of "it works in the image but not when I mount".
